title: Constitutional & Administrative Law - Syllabus Gap Pack (UGC NET Law)
note: Fills gaps: Arts 12-32 case law, Parliament/Union executive, Centre-State & finance, services, elections, special provisions and administrative law.

questions.question: In Zee Telefilms Ltd. v. Union of India (2005), the Supreme Court held that the BCCI:

options.A: Is 'State' under Art. 12 because it controls a national sport
options.B: Is 'State' only for the purposes of Art. 14
options.C: Is not 'State' under Art. 12, though its public-duty actions may still be amenable to writ jurisdiction under Art. 226
options.D: Is a statutory body created under the Societies Registration Act and hence 'State'

questions.explanation: By a 3:2 majority the BCCI was held not to be 'State', but writs may lie for enforcement of public duties.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The doctrine of eclipse applies to pre-constitutional laws that are inconsistent with Part III.
Reason (R): Such laws are void ab initio under Art. 13(1) and cannot be revived.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Pre-constitutional laws are only overshadowed (dormant), not dead (Bhikaji Narain Dhakras); Deep Chand/Mahendra Lal Jaini treat post-constitutional laws as void ab initio.

questions.question:
Which of the following Fundamental Rights are expressly available against private individuals also?
1. Art. 15(2) - access to shops, hotels, wells
2. Art. 17 - abolition of untouchability
3. Art. 23 - prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
4. Art. 20(1) - protection against ex post facto laws

options.A: 2, 3 and 4 only
options.B: 1, 3 and 4 only
options.D: 1 and 4 only

questions.explanation: Art. 20 protects only against State action (conviction under law).

questions.question: In Maqbool Hussain v. State of Bombay (1953), the Supreme Court held that confiscation by Sea Customs authorities did NOT bar a later criminal trial under Art. 20(2) because:

options.A: Art. 20(2) applies only to civil penalties
options.B: The Customs authorities were not a court or judicial tribunal, so there was no 'prosecution and punishment'
options.C: The offence was different in character
options.D: Double jeopardy applies only to offences under the IPC

questions.explanation: Art. 20(2) requires prosecution and punishment before a court or judicial tribunal.

questions.question: Under Art. 22(4), preventive detention beyond ___ requires the report of an Advisory Board (unless Parliament acts under Art. 22(7)). The reduction of this period by the 44th Amendment has:

options.A: Six months; been brought into force in 1978
options.B: Two months; been in force since 1979
options.C: Three months; been replaced by six months by the 44th Amendment
options.D: Three months; not been brought into force

questions.explanation: The original three-month period still applies as the 44th Amendment's change to two months was never notified.

questions.question: Which decision held that the 'right to die' is not part of Art. 21 and overruled P. Rathinam v. Union of India?

options.A: Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India
options.B: Maruti Shripati Dubal v. State of Maharashtra
options.C: Common Cause v. Union of India
options.D: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab

questions.explanation: Gian Kaur (1996, 5 judges) upheld s.309 IPC and rejected a right to die; Common Cause (2018) allowed passive euthanasia/living wills.

questions.question: The doctrine of 'essential religious practices' was first articulated in:

options.A: Commissioner, H.R.E., Madras v. Sri Lakshmindra Thirtha Swamiar of Sri Shirur Mutt
options.B: Durgah Committee, Ajmer v. Syed Hussain Ali
options.C: Sardar Syedna Taher Saifuddin v. State of Bombay
options.D: S.P. Mittal v. Union of India

questions.explanation: Shirur Mutt (1954) held that what constitutes an essential part of a religion is to be decided with reference to its doctrines.

questions.question: In its 2024 seven-judge decision on the minority status of Aligarh Muslim University, the Supreme Court:

options.A: Held AMU is a minority institution as it was established by Muslims
options.B: Overruled the reasoning in S. Azeez Basha, holding that an institution does not lose minority character merely because it was incorporated by statute, and left the final determination to a regular Bench
options.C: Unanimously reaffirmed S. Azeez Basha v. Union of India
options.D: Held Art. 30(1) does not apply to universities

questions.explanation: The decision was 4:3; the test looks to who established the institution and for whom, not mere statutory incorporation.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A writ of certiorari under Art. 226 lies against judicial orders of civil courts.
Reason (R): In Radhey Shyam v. Chhabi Nath (2015), the Supreme Court held that orders of civil courts are amenable to supervisory jurisdiction under Art. 227 and not to writ of certiorari.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Radhey Shyam overruled Surya Dev Rai; judicial orders of civil courts can be corrected under Art. 227 only.

questions.question: State of West Bengal v. Anwar Ali Sarkar (1952) struck down the West Bengal Special Courts Act, 1950 because:

options.A: It created courts without legislative competence
options.B: It violated the right to counsel under Art. 22
options.C: It vested uncontrolled discretion in the Government to refer cases to Special Courts without a guiding policy, violating Art. 14
options.D: It authorised ex post facto punishment

questions.explanation: The Act lacked an intelligible differentia and a nexus; classification was left to executive discretion.

questions.question: Basheshar Nath v. CIT (1959) is associated with the proposition that:

options.A: Only Art. 19 rights may be waived
options.B: A citizen can waive any fundamental right by contract
options.C: Fundamental rights cannot be waived by a citizen, as they are a constitutional policy
options.D: Waiver is possible only before a court

questions.explanation: The majority held Art. 14 rights cannot be waived.

questions.question: In Sri Venkataramana Devaru v. State of Mysore (1958), the Supreme Court resolved a conflict between Art. 25(2)(b) and Art. 26(b) by:

options.A: Holding Art. 26(b) absolute
options.B: Applying the rule of harmonious construction, holding that the denominational right under Art. 26(b) is subject to the right of all Hindus to enter temples under Art. 25(2)(b)
options.D: Striking down the impugned Act

questions.explanation: Harmonious construction gives effect to both provisions as far as possible.

questions.question: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (implementing Art. 39A), an award of a Lok Adalat is:

options.A: Deemed a decree of a civil court, final and binding, with no appeal against it
options.B: Appealable to the High Court
options.C: A mere recommendation requiring court confirmation
options.D: Enforceable only through arbitration

questions.explanation: Section 21 of the Act.

questions.question: In Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India (1995), the Supreme Court:

options.A: Held that a Hindu husband converting to Islam to remarry commits bigamy under s.494 IPC, and urged the State to implement Art. 44
options.B: Upheld Muslim personal law on polygamy for all communities
options.D: Held that Art. 44 is a fundamental right

questions.explanation: The Court said conversion does not dissolve the first marriage and called for a Uniform Civil Code.

questions.question: The fundamental duty 'to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform' is contained in Art. 51A:

options.A: Clause (g)
options.B: Clause (h)
options.D: Clause (j)

questions.explanation: (g) environment; (i) public property and violence; (j) individual and collective excellence.

questions.question:
Match the Directive Principle with its Article.
List I:
1. Art. 40
2. Art. 43A
3. Art. 49
4. Art. 50
List II:
a. Separation of judiciary from the executive
b. Organisation of village panchayats
c. Participation of workers in management
d. Protection of monuments of national importance
questions.explanation: Art. 43A was added by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.question: In Property Owners Association v. State of Maharashtra (2024), a nine-judge Bench held on Art. 39(b) that:

options.A: Not every privately owned resource is a material resource of the community; some may qualify depending on factors such as nature, scarcity and impact on the community, and the earlier wide view of Krishna Iyer J. was not accepted
options.B: Every privately owned resource is a 'material resource of the community'
options.C: Art. 39(b) applies only to natural resources
options.D: Art. 31C is no longer valid

questions.explanation: The majority rejected the wide 'socialist' reading from Ranganatha Reddy / Sanjeev Coke.

questions.question: In S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab (2001), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: A non-member can be repeatedly appointed Minister for successive six-month terms
options.B: Ministers need not be members of the legislature at all
options.C: A person who is not a member of the legislature cannot be appointed Minister again for a second consecutive term without being elected
options.D: Art. 164(4) does not apply to Chief Ministers

questions.explanation: Repeated appointment without election defeats the purpose of Art. 164(4).

questions.question:
Consider the Attorney General of India:
1. He is appointed by the President.
2. He must be a person qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court.
3. He can be removed only by impeachment like a Judge.
4. He has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.

options.A: 1, 2 and 4 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 3 and 4 only

questions.explanation: He holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art. 76).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Comptroller and Auditor General can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
Reason (R): This safeguard protects the independence of the CAG from the executive.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Art. 148(1): removal like a Supreme Court Judge secures independence.

questions.question: The Vice-President of India can be removed by:

options.A: A resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, after 14 days' notice
options.B: A two-thirds majority in both Houses in joint sitting
options.C: Impeachment by Parliament as for the President
options.D: A resolution of the Rajya Sabha by two-thirds of members present and voting

questions.explanation: Art. 67(b) - 'effective majority' in Rajya Sabha and simple majority in Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following Bills was NOT enacted at a joint sitting of the two Houses under Art. 108?

options.A: Dowry Prohibition Bill, 1960
options.B: Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill, 1977
options.D: Citizenship (Amendment) Bill, 2019

questions.explanation: Joint sittings have been held only three times.

questions.question: In the Aadhaar case (Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India, 2018), the Supreme Court by majority:

options.A: Held the Aadhaar Act could not be certified as a Money Bill
options.B: Held the Aadhaar Act was validly passed as a Money Bill under Art. 110(1)(a)
options.C: Declined to examine the Speaker's certification
options.D: Referred the Money Bill question to a seven-judge Bench

questions.explanation: Chandrachud J dissented, calling the Money Bill route a fraud on the Constitution.

questions.question:
Consider a Money Bill:
1. It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
2. It can be introduced only on the recommendation of the President.
3. The Rajya Sabha may only make recommendations, to be returned within 14 days.
4. It can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha with the Speaker's certificate.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.B: 1, 3 and 4 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 4 only

questions.question: In Tej Kiran Jain v. N. Sanjiva Reddy (1970), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: Art. 105(2) immunity extends only to relevant speeches
options.B: Immunity does not extend to members' written submissions
options.C: Courts may review the content of speeches
options.D: Art. 105(2) gives absolute immunity for anything said in Parliament, even if defamatory

questions.explanation: The words 'anything said' were given their full meaning.

questions.question: In Keisham Meghachandra Singh v. Speaker, Manipur Legislative Assembly (2020), the Supreme Court:

options.A: Held the Speaker's disqualification power is non-justiciable
options.B: Held that a Speaker cannot belong to a political party
options.D: Directed that the Speaker should ordinarily decide Tenth Schedule petitions within three months and suggested Parliament consider an independent tribunal

questions.explanation: The Court urged Parliament to reconsider vesting adjudication in the Speaker.

questions.question: In Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006), the Supreme Court:

options.A: Upheld the amendment removing the domicile requirement and introducing open ballot for Rajya Sabha elections
options.B: Struck down open ballot in Rajya Sabha elections
options.C: Held that Rajya Sabha elections must be by direct vote
options.D: Declared that federalism bars non-resident members

questions.explanation: The right to vote in Rajya Sabha elections is statutory, not fundamental.

questions.question: Under Art. 171, the Legislative Council of a State shall have not more than ___ of the Assembly's total membership and not less than ___ members (except J&K earlier).

options.A: One-third; 60
options.B: One-half; 40
options.D: One-fourth; 30

questions.explanation: Art. 169 allows creation/abolition by Parliament on the Assembly's special majority resolution; it is not an Art. 368 amendment.

questions.question: The repeated re-promulgation of ordinances without placing them before the Legislature was held to be a 'fraud on the Constitution' in:

options.A: T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
options.B: Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India
options.C: A.K. Roy v. Union of India
options.D: D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar

questions.explanation: The Bihar Governor had re-promulgated ordinances for years; Krishna Kumar Singh (2017) affirmed the principle.

questions.question: In State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor of Punjab (2023), the Supreme Court held that a Governor:

options.A: Can withhold assent indefinitely
options.B: Cannot sit on Bills; if he withholds assent under Art. 200 he must return the Bill with a message 'as soon as possible'
options.D: Has absolute discretion in reserving Bills

questions.explanation: Indefinite inaction defeats the legislative process and parliamentary democracy.

questions.question: In Subhash Desai v. Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra (2023), the Supreme Court:

options.A: Held the Governor's call for a floor test was unjustified for lack of objective material, but did not restore the status quo ante because the Chief Minister had resigned without facing it
options.B: Reinstated the resigned Chief Minister
options.C: Upheld the Speaker's choice of Whip
options.D: Held the floor test is mandatory in all cases

questions.explanation: The Court also referred the Nabam Rebia decision to a larger Bench.

questions.question: Under s.12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, the maximum punishment for contempt of court is:

options.A: Imprisonment up to two years
options.B: Imprisonment up to one year or fine up to Rs 5,000
options.C: Simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs 2,000, or both
options.D: Fine up to Rs 10,000 only

questions.explanation: An apology may be accepted in discharge or remission of punishment.

questions.question: Which reference under Art. 143 was returned unanswered by the Supreme Court?

options.A: Re Berubari Union
options.B: Re Keshav Singh
options.D: Special Reference No. 1 of 1993 (Ayodhya reference)

questions.explanation: In Dr. M. Ismail Faruqui v. Union of India (1994) the Court declined to answer the reference.

questions.question: The first Judge against whom a motion for removal (impeachment) was moved in the Lok Sabha was:

options.A: Justice Soumitra Sen
options.B: Justice P.D. Dinakaran
options.D: Justice S.K. Gangele

questions.explanation: The 1993 motion failed for want of the required majority of total membership.

questions.question: In State of West Bengal v. Nripendra Nath Bagchi (1966), the Supreme Court held that 'control' over subordinate courts under Art. 235 includes:

options.A: Only transfers and postings
options.B: Only the power to recommend promotions
options.D: Disciplinary control including the power to dismiss, remove or reduce in rank, vested in the High Court

questions.explanation: The High Court's control is exclusive of the executive.

questions.question: In Prem Chand Garg v. Excise Commissioner, U.P. (1962), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: Art. 142 can override Fundamental Rights
options.B: An order under Art. 142 cannot contravene the Fundamental Rights, and Supreme Court rules cannot abridge the free exercise of Art. 32
options.D: Security deposits for writs are valid

questions.explanation: A rule requiring security deposit for Art. 32 petitions was struck down.

questions.question: Under the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019, the maximum strength of the Supreme Court (including the CJI) is:
questions.explanation: It was raised from 31 to 34 in 2019 (verify for any later change).

questions.question:
Match the Article with the circumstance in which Parliament may legislate on a State List subject.
List I:
1. Art. 249
2. Art. 250
3. Art. 252
4. Art. 253
List II:
a. Rajya Sabha resolution (2/3 present and voting) in national interest
b. Proclamation of Emergency in operation
c. Resolution of legislatures of two or more States
d. Implementation of treaties and international agreements
questions.explanation: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Art. 249 lasts one year and is renewable.

questions.question: In Union of India v. H.S. Dhillon (1971), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: Parliament's residuary power under Art. 248 and Entry 97 of List I extends to taxation of matters not mentioned in List II or III
options.B: Parliament has no residuary power of taxation
options.D: Entry 97 is limited to non-fiscal laws

questions.explanation: The wealth tax on agricultural land value was upheld as a matter outside List II.

questions.question: Under Art. 365, the President may hold that the constitutional machinery in a State has failed where the State:

options.A: Fails to implement central schemes
options.B: Fails to comply with or give effect to directions given by the Union in exercise of its executive power
options.D: Violates fiscal discipline

questions.explanation: Art. 365 operates alongside Art. 356.

questions.question: Which of the following owes its constitutional basis to a specific Article (Art. 263)?

options.A: Zonal Councils
options.B: Inter-State Council
options.D: National Development Council

questions.explanation: Zonal Councils were created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956; the Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 under Art. 263.

questions.question: Under Art. 280, the President constitutes a Finance Commission at the expiration of every fifth year or earlier, consisting of:

options.A: A Chairman and two other members
options.B: A Chairman and four other members
options.C: A Chairman and six other members
options.D: The Finance Minister and four members

questions.explanation: The qualifications of members are prescribed by Parliament.

questions.question: In Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd. (2022), the Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations are:

options.A: Binding on Union and States
options.B: Binding on the Union only
options.C: Only persuasive, as Parliament and State legislatures have simultaneous power under Art. 246A
options.D: Mandatory for State legislatures

questions.explanation: The Court emphasised cooperative federalism.

questions.question: Under Art. 289(2), the Union may tax the trade or business of a State only if:

options.A: The State consents
options.B: The Finance Commission recommends
options.D: Parliament by law so provides

questions.explanation: Art. 289(1) otherwise exempts State property and income from Union taxation.

questions.question: In Vidya Devi v. State of Himachal Pradesh (2020), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: Right to property has no constitutional basis after the 44th Amendment
options.B: The State can acquire property without law
options.C: The right to property is a constitutional and human right under Art. 300A, and the State cannot deprive a person of property without authority of law or claim title by adverse possession
options.D: Art. 300A requires full market compensation

questions.explanation: A welfare State cannot invoke adverse possession against a citizen.

questions.question: Automobile Transport (Rajasthan) Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan (1962) is associated with:

options.A: Prohibition on all taxes under Art. 301
options.B: Cession of territory
options.D: The concept of compensatory taxes not hampering freedom of trade under Art. 301

questions.explanation: Taxes charged for use of facilities are not restrictions on trade.

questions.question: Under Art. 304(b), a Bill imposing reasonable restrictions on trade in a State in the public interest:

options.A: Requires the Governor's recommendation
options.B: Can be introduced only with the previous sanction of the President
options.D: Can be introduced freely

questions.explanation: The proviso to Art. 304(b).

questions.question: In GVK Industries Ltd. v. ITO (2011), the Supreme Court held that Parliament's power to make extra-territorial laws under Art. 245(2):

options.A: Exists but requires a nexus with India (territorial nexus)
options.B: Is unlimited
options.D: Is available only to States

questions.explanation: State legislatures do not have extra-territorial power but may legislate with nexus.

questions.question: Under Art. 246A(2), the power to make laws on GST where supply of goods or services occurs in the course of inter-State trade or commerce lies with:

options.A: The State legislatures exclusively
options.B: Both concurrently
options.D: The GST Council

questions.explanation: Art. 246A(1) gives simultaneous power otherwise.

questions.question: Under Art. 271, a surcharge levied on taxes referred to in Arts. 269 and 270:

options.A: Is shared with the States
options.B: Is wholly retained by the Union
options.D: Is referred to the Finance Commission

questions.explanation: Cesses and surcharges are not part of the divisible pool.

questions.question: In Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985), the Constitution Bench held that:

options.A: The provisos to Art. 311(2) are unconstitutional
options.B: Pleasure doctrine is absolute
options.C: The exceptions in the second proviso to Art. 311(2) are valid, but reasons for dispensing with the inquiry must be recorded in writing and are subject to judicial review
options.D: Art. 311 applies to the armed forces fully

questions.explanation: Natural justice may be excluded where holding an inquiry is not reasonably practicable.

questions.question: In B.P. Singhal v. Union of India (2010), the Supreme Court held that the President's pleasure to remove a Governor:

options.A: Is not unfettered; removal needs compelling reasons, and cannot be for a change of Government
options.B: Is unfettered
options.D: Requires CJI consultation

questions.explanation: Reasons need not be disclosed unless prima facie mala fides is shown.

questions.question: Under Art. 312(3), the All-India Judicial Service shall not include any post inferior to:

options.A: Civil Judge (Junior Division)
options.B: Additional District Judge
options.D: Chief Judicial Magistrate

questions.explanation: Art. 312(1) requires a Rajya Sabha resolution by two-thirds present and voting.

questions.question: Under Art. 316, a member of the UPSC holds office for ___ years or until age ___; a member of a State PSC for six years or age ___, whichever is earlier.
N.P. Ponnuswami v. Returning Officer, Namakkal (1952) laid down that:

options.A: Art. 329(b) bars courts from interfering in the election process once it has begun, relief being by election petition after the election
options.B: Courts may interfere with any stage of the election process
options.C: Election disputes lie under Art. 32 only
options.D: Rejection of nomination can always be challenged by writ

questions.explanation: Art. 329(b) is a non obstante bar.

questions.question: Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner (1978) explained that Art. 324:

options.A: Is a plenary residuary power which can fill gaps where law is silent, but cannot override law and must be exercised fairly
options.B: Is subordinate to the Representation of the People Act
options.D: Applies only to Parliament elections

questions.explanation: Art. 324 is supplementary to enacted law.

questions.question: Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) is notable for:

options.A: Upholding s.8(4) of the Representation of the People Act
options.B: Introducing NOTA
options.C: Striking down s.8(4) RPA, so a convicted legislator sentenced to two or more years is disqualified immediately
options.D: Mandating disclosure of assets

questions.explanation: The protection of three months/appeal for sitting members was invalid.

questions.question: In Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: Leases of tribal land to private parties are valid
options.B: The Governor cannot regulate land transfer
options.C: The Fifth Schedule applies to Assam
options.D: Transfer or lease of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals and private companies is void under the Fifth Schedule

questions.explanation: The State is a 'person' for the purpose of para 5(2) of the Fifth Schedule.

questions.question: In Re: Article 370 (2023), the Constitution Bench held that:

options.A: Art. 370 was a temporary provision, and the President could issue the 2019 notification under Art. 370(3) even after the Constituent Assembly of J&K ceased to exist
options.B: Art. 370 was a permanent provision
options.C: The J&K Reorganisation Act was invalid
options.D: Ladakh could not be made a Union Territory

questions.explanation: The recommendation of the Constituent Assembly was not binding on the President.

questions.question: Under Art. 348(2), the Governor, with the previous consent of the President, may authorise the use of Hindi or another State official language in:

options.A: Proceedings of the High Court, though not its judgments, decrees or orders
options.B: Judgments, decrees and orders of the High Court
options.D: Parliament

questions.explanation: The proviso excludes judgments, decrees and orders.

questions.question: Art. 340 enables the President to appoint a Commission to investigate the conditions of backward classes. The first such Commission was:

options.A: Mandal Commission (1979)
options.B: Swaran Singh Commission
options.D: Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953)

questions.explanation: The second was the B.P. Mandal Commission (1979).

questions.question: Under Art. 371A, an Act of Parliament affecting which of the following does not apply to Nagaland unless its Legislative Assembly so resolves?

options.A: Citizenship
options.B: Defence of India
options.D: Naga customary law and procedure, and ownership and transfer of land and resources

questions.explanation: Art. 371A(1)(a) also covers religious or social practices of the Nagas.

questions.question: In In Re: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 (2024), the Constitution Bench by a 4:1 majority:

options.A: Struck down s.6A
options.B: Held it violated Art. 29
options.C: Upheld s.6A, which grants citizenship to migrants from Bangladesh who entered Assam before 25 March 1971
options.D: Fixed the cut-off at 1951

questions.explanation: Pardiwala J dissented.

questions.question:
Arrange the following cases on Art. 356 and State Governments in chronological order:
P. S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Q. State of Rajasthan v. Union of India
R. Nabam Rebia v. Deputy Speaker
S. Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India

options.A: Q-P-S-R
options.B: P-Q-S-R
options.D: Q-P-R-S

questions.question: In Ram Jawaya Kapur v. State of Punjab (1955), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: India follows strict separation of powers
options.B: The executive cannot act without a law
options.C: The Indian Constitution does not recognise separation of powers in its absolute rigidity, and executive power is co-extensive with legislative power unless restricted
options.D: Textbook nationalisation was unconstitutional

questions.explanation: This is the leading case on the Indian approach to separation of powers.

questions.question: The maxim delegatus non potest delegare in administrative law means that a delegate:

options.A: Can freely sub-delegate
options.B: May delegate to courts
options.C: Cannot sub-delegate unless authorised by the parent statute (Ganpati Singhji v. State of Ajmer)
options.D: Must be elected

questions.explanation: Sub-delegation requires express or necessarily implied authority.

questions.question: In Padfield v. Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (1968), the House of Lords held that:

options.A: Ministerial discretion is unfettered
options.B: Discretion must be exercised to promote the policy and objects of the Act, and refusal without reason may be quashed
options.D: Ministers need no reasons

questions.explanation: No discretion is truly unfettered.

questions.question: In Subramanian Swamy v. Director, CBI (2014), a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court:

options.A: Struck down s.6A of the DSPE Act (prior sanction to investigate officers of Joint Secretary level and above) as violative of Art. 14
options.B: Upheld s.6A of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act as a valid classification
options.D: Held prior sanction is required for all public servants

questions.explanation: Section 6A (the 'Single Directive' statutorily revived in 2003) created an unreasonable classification among corruption-accused public servants and was struck down under Art. 14.

questions.question: In Om Kumar v. Union of India (2001), the Supreme Court stated that the doctrine of proportionality:

options.A: Never applies in India
options.B: Applies only to penalties
options.D: Applies where fundamental rights are affected (primary review), while Wednesbury unreasonableness applies to ordinary administrative action (secondary review)

questions.explanation: Proportionality is a stricter standard of review.

questions.question: In Union of India v. Hindustan Development Corporation (1993), the Supreme Court held that legitimate expectation:

options.A: Is an enforceable right in all cases
options.B: Is a Fundamental Right
options.D: Is not a legal right by itself, but denial of a reasonable expectation arbitrarily may be reviewed; it cannot override public interest

questions.explanation: It operates as a ground of review under Art. 14.

questions.question: In S.N. Mukherjee v. Union of India (1990), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: Administrative authorities need not give reasons
options.B: Reasons are needed only for judicial decisions
options.C: Reasons must be recorded for administrative decisions with civil consequences, unless a statute excludes it, including by a confirming authority under the Army Act
options.D: Reasons are needed only in service matters

questions.explanation: The duty to give reasons is part of natural justice.

questions.question: Syed Yakoob v. K.S. Radhakrishnan (1964) held that a writ of certiorari:

options.A: Is an appeal on facts
options.B: Is available against private bodies in all cases
options.C: Can reverse findings of fact freely
options.D: Is supervisory and can correct errors of jurisdiction and errors of law apparent on the face of the record, but not errors of fact

questions.explanation: Certiorari is not an appellate remedy.

questions.question: Which statement distinguishes the writs of prohibition and certiorari?

options.A: Prohibition is issued to prevent an inferior body from exceeding jurisdiction while proceedings are pending; certiorari quashes an order already made
options.B: Prohibition is issued after the order, certiorari before it
options.C: Both are issued against private persons
options.D: Both are issued against administrative bodies only

questions.explanation: Both lie only against judicial or quasi-judicial authorities.

questions.question: The first reported Public Interest Litigation case in India is generally considered to be:

options.A: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
options.B: Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar
options.C: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
options.D: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India

questions.explanation: It concerned under-trial prisoners and established the right to speedy trial under Art. 21.

questions.question: Bhikraj Jaipuria v. Union of India (1962) is associated with Art. 299(1), which requires that contracts made in the exercise of the executive power of the Union or a State be:

options.A: Expressed to be made by the President/Governor and executed on their behalf by persons authorised, and these formalities are mandatory
options.B: Oral if urgent
options.D: Registered under the Contract Act

questions.explanation: Non-compliance makes the contract unenforceable against the Government.

questions.question: S.P. Sampath Kumar v. Union of India (1987) upheld the exclusion of High Court jurisdiction by the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985; this view was later overruled in:

options.A: Kesavananda Bharati
options.B: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India
options.D: S.R. Bommai

questions.explanation: L. Chandra Kumar (1997) held judicial review by High Courts is part of the basic structure.

questions.question: In Ram Krishna Dalmia v. Justice S.R. Tendolkar (1958), the Supreme Court held that a Commission of Inquiry under the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952:

options.A: Can pass binding judgments
options.B: Can punish for contempt of Parliament
options.D: Is a fact-finding body whose findings are not binding and have no legal consequence by themselves

questions.explanation: The Act was upheld; the Commission only advises.

questions.question: In Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court:

options.A: Dismissed the petition
options.B: Held the CVC cannot supervise the CBI
options.D: Gave the CVC statutory status and prescribed a minimum two-year tenure for the CBI Director, and invalidated the 'Single Directive' requiring prior sanction to investigate senior officers

questions.explanation: The 'Single Directive' was later invoked again as s.6A DSPE Act, struck down in Subramanian Swamy (2014).

questions.question: In CPIO, Supreme Court of India v. Subhash Chandra Agarwal (2019), the Constitution Bench held that:

options.A: The Office of the Chief Justice of India is outside the RTI Act
options.B: The Office of the CJI is a public authority under the RTI Act, and transparency is compatible with judicial independence
options.C: RTI does not apply to the judiciary at all
options.D: Only the Registry is a public authority

questions.explanation: Personal information was subject to the fiduciary and privacy exemptions.

questions.question: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Lokpal's jurisdiction over the Prime Minister excludes allegations relating to:

options.A: Corruption in office
options.B: Cabinet decisions
options.D: International relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space

questions.explanation: Inquiry against the PM needs approval of two-thirds of the full Lokpal bench and is held in camera.

questions.question:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
P. K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
Q. Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
R. Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
S. Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar

options.A: Q-S-R-P
options.B: S-Q-R-P
options.D: S-Q-P-R

questions.question:
Match the case with its holding.
List I:
1. Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
2. Joseph Shine v. Union of India
3. NALSA v. Union of India
4. K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
List II:
a. Right to privacy is a Fundamental Right
b. Decriminalised consensual same-sex acts under s.377 IPC
c. Struck down s.497 IPC (adultery)
d. Recognition of transgender persons as a 'third gender'
questions.explanation: Navtej and Joseph Shine are 2018; NALSA 2014; Puttaswamy 2017.

questions.question: In Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala (Sabarimala, 2018), the Judge who dissented in the 4:1 verdict was:

options.A: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud
options.B: Justice A.M. Khanwilkar
options.D: Justice Indu Malhotra

questions.explanation: Indu Malhotra J held that courts should not interfere in matters of religious faith.

questions.question: In Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar (1962), the Supreme Court:

options.A: Struck down s.124A IPC
options.B: Upheld s.124A IPC but limited it to acts having a tendency or intention to create public disorder or incite violence
options.D: Held s.124A violates Art. 14

questions.explanation: S.G. Vombatkere (2022) kept s.124A in abeyance; BNS s.152 replaced it.

questions.question: In Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme because it:

options.A: Violated Art. 21A
options.B: Violated the voters' right to information under Art. 19(1)(a)
options.D: Lacked Presidential assent

questions.explanation: The Court held unlimited anonymous corporate funding violates free and fair elections.

questions.question: In Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India (2023), a Constitution Bench held that the Delhi Government has legislative and executive control over 'services' except:

options.A: Revenue and finance
options.B: Education and health
options.D: Water and electricity

questions.explanation: The Union later enacted the GNCTD (Amendment) Act, 2023.

questions.question: In Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: Internet access is not protected
options.B: Art. 19(2) is inapplicable to the internet
options.D: Freedom of speech and trade through the internet is protected under Arts. 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g), and indefinite suspension of the internet is impermissible

questions.explanation: Restrictions must satisfy proportionality and be published.
